{{Quote|The Kaikielii had been a key power at the dawn of the Republic, and its governors accepted homage from numerous colony planets — Ruan, the moons of Jonsior, even Foerost. But over the millennia, these achieved full membership and shifting fate left the hub behind.|Dr. [[Gabrel Treon]], "[[Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji: A Cartel of Genes]]," [[Byblos Journal of Historical Science]], [[104 ABY]]|<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />}}
'''Kaikielius''' was a planet in the [[Kaikielius system/Legends|Kaikielius system]] of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="DESB" /> A regional power before the rise of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] and a [[Core Founder/Legends|Core Founder]],<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" /> it was situated on the [[Koros Trunk Line/Legends|Koros Trunk Line]], just outside of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]].<ref name="TEA" /> The planet was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the influential political dynasty [[House Praji/Legends|House Praji]].<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

==Description==
{{Quote|If Coruscant was the galaxy's urban center, the reimagined Kaikielius was a cookie-cutter suburb.|Dr. Gabrel Treon, "Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji: A Cartel of Genes"|<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />}}
Kaikielius was located on the [[Koros Trunk Line/Legends|Koros Trunk Line]] between [[Foerost/Legends|Foerost]] and [[Ruan]], linking [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to the [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]]-producing worlds of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]].<ref name="BatDC" /> The planet occupied a strategically vital position that throughout history made it a target for fleets seeking to conquer Coruscant, whether from the Deep Core or from the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]] via the [[Agricultural Circuit]].<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" /><ref name="TEA" />

Historically, Kaikielius was a rural and pastoral world, with the planetary capital based at [[Kesipli]]. The planet was [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|heavily urbanized]] after [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]] in a desperate attempt to compete economically with the [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Empress Teta system]], and became known for poverty, pollution, and urban decay. "[[Ring-city|Ring-cities]]" developed as [[Mayor/Legends|mayors]] walled off city centers in an effort to contain crime while construction continued to expand in concentric rings of development.<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

Following the [[Kaikieli Reconquista]] of [[4225 BBY]] and the destruction of most of the planet's criminal elements, Kaikielius was largely restored and became described as the gentrified suburb to Coruscant's urban center.<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

==History==
===Pre-Republic era===
The planet was settled sometime between [[25,200 BBY]] and [[25,053 BBY]] by [[Human/Legends|Humans]] after the fall of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]]. The locals were known as Kaikielii. An aristocratic world, Kaikielius was ruled by the [[Noble/Legends|noble]] [[Great House]]s, of which the oldest and most prominent were the [[Triad (Great Houses)|Triad]] of [[House Praji/Legends|House Praji]], [[House Vahali/Legends|House Vahali]], and [[House Juoni]], with lesser houses vying for patronage. Before the rise of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], Kaikielius had held suzerainty over [[Ruan]], the [[moons of Jonsior]], and [[Foerost/Legends|Foerost]].<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

An early ruler of the planet was [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Tyler Sapius Praji]], who was a signatory of the [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|Galactic Constitution]], bringing Kaikielius into the Galactic Republic as a [[Core Founder/Legends|Core Founder]].<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

===The early Republic===
The Triad had a powerful voice on Coruscant in the early years of the Galactic Republic, with the Prajii having the most influence. During the [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|Alsakan Conflicts]], Kaikielius sided with Coruscant, and House Juoni lost virtually all of its power after it sided with [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]] during the [[First Alsakan Conflict]] of [[17,000 BBY]]: its [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]] holdings were destroyed by [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|orbital bombardment]], and Kaikielius was left to the control of the Prajii and the Vahalii.<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

Kaikielius slowly faded from [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] political importance in the years after the [[Corellian Interregnal]], and its colonies became full Republic members in their own right. From [[11,000 BBY]] it rivaled [[Koros]] for influence in the Core Worlds, but infighting in the Koros system, and between the Great Houses on Kaikielius, prevented either from gaining an advantage. In 5000 BBY, however, the nine planets of the Koros system were [[Unification Wars (Koros)/Legends|unified]] by [[Teta/Legends|Empress Teta]], and she subsequently gained much favor with Coruscant for her actions in repelling the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] during the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]. Kaikielius suffered an attack by [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow's]] fleet in this war,<ref name="TEA" /> and within a hundred years of the war's conclusion, Koros had eclipsed it in power and influence.<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

===Decline===
In a frantic attempt to compete with Koros, Kaikielius underwent rapid urbanization, which devastated the countryside and left ancient city cores neglected, decayed and abandoned. Wealthy citizens abandoned the city centers in favor of the exurbs or left the planet altogether. Corrupt [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] developers and [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] criminal cartels moved into the poverty-stricken city centers, while mayors walled off the city cores and cut off utilities in a desperate effort to contain crime and poverty. Kaikielius' [[Ring-city|ring-cities]] became infamous as the city cores were abandoned to anarchy while construction continued to expand in concentric rings of development.<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

Kaikielius suffered devastating [[Groundquake/Legends|groundquakes]] during the [[Quake Years]] around [[4800 BBY]], after which House Praji decamped to Coruscant, leaving rule of the increasingly ungovernable planet to House Vahali. The Vahalii soon dominated all aspects of Kaikielius' government, but the system was effectively under the control of Hutt [[Kajidic/Legends|''kajidics'']] and became a haven for [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]]: the approach to the [[Kaikielius system/Legends|Kaikielius system]] on the Koros Trunk Line became known as "[[Butcher's Alley]]" for the death toll. The Prajii were content to let their rivals destroy themselves before they moved in to pick up the pieces. Indeed, [[Emppu Praji-Barck]], who served as a Republic [[Minister of State]] for sixty years, continually filibustered [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] debates on intervention in the Kaikielius system.<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

===Recovery===
It was not until [[4225 BBY]] that the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] on [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]] sent a task force to end the Hutts' domination over the planet: the Republic had discovered that the [[Odominic]] ''kajidic'' had been supplying weapons to both sides in the war between gangs and [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|police]] on Kaikielius. Now a matter of Republic security rather than one of law enforcement, the planet's criminal elements were ousted through the military might of a joint Republic-Jedi expedition known as the [[Kaikieli Reconquista]]. The [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Derrica Praji]] was one of the commanders of the expedition, to the fury of his relatives. During the course of the Reconquista, Derrica discovered evidence in [[Kesipli]] that his great-aunt, Emppu Praji-Barck, had committed sedition in urging the Odominic to supply both sides of the gang war. For the sake of his family, Derrica destroyed the evidence, though House Praji's objective of seizing sole power on Kaikielius had come to naught.<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

In the aftermath of the Reconquista, Kaikielius was rebuilt with Republic aid, becoming a prosperous, "cookie-cutter suburb" to Coruscant's urban center. The Prajii left the Vahalii to rule Kaikielius while they further solidified power on Coruscant.<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

Over the millennia, Kaikielius was [[Battle of Kaikielius (Great Sith War)|attacked]] by [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] in the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], [[Battle of Kaikielius (Great Galactic War)|again]] by the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]] during the [[Great Galactic War]], and by [[Skere Kaan]] during the [[New Sith Wars]], all seeking to claim the approach to Coruscant.<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

===The Clone Wars===
The [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] [[Kaikielius campaign|took the world]] as part of [[Operation Durge's Lance]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" /> A footnote to the Kaikielius campaign was the curious case of the "[[Mad Clone of Kaikielius]]," an aberrant [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] who suddenly went berserk during the battle and turned his [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] on his squadmates, who he later insisted had been replaced by Separatist [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]].<ref name="Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-9-battlfields-of-the-clone-wars|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 9: Battlefields of the Clone Wars}}</ref>

[[Refugee/Legends|Refugees]] from Kaikielius displaced by the Separatist invasion were resettled on [[Byss/Legends|Byss]] in the Deep Core. Nominally a recolonization effort, the planet in fact became the secret retreat for [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and his [[Dark Side Elite]] under the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and the colonists were slowly [[Force drain/Legends|drained]] of their life energies to sustain the Emperor and his adepts.<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

===The Galactic Civil War and after===
Following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] and the formation of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], Kaikielius surrendered to [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar's]] fleet as it entered the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] in [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]] in preparation for the [[Core Campaign]].<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

In [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]], Kaikielius was [[Battle of Kaikielius (Galactic Civil War)|attacked]] by Imperial forces led by [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Nahdonnis Praji]], advancing out of the Deep Core as part of the Reborn Emperor's [[Pre–Shadow Hand campaign|reconquest]]. House Vahali's [[Skyhook/Legends|skyhook]] was destroyed by Praji's fleet and he placed the planet under martial law. This battle, along with a [[Battle of Metellos (Galactic Civil War)|strike]] against [[Metellos/Legends|Metellos]], persuaded the leaders of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] that they could not hold the capital on Coruscant. The New Republic's command staff abandoned the galactic capital for the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

The clone Emperor appointed Praji [[Governor-General/Legends|Governor-General]] of the world.<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" /> Soon after, commanders loyal to the [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Imperial Ruling Council]] [[Second Battle of Coruscant|recaptured Coruscant]], but disagreements between commanders sparked the bloody [[Imperial Civil War]], laying much of the capital to waste.<ref name="DESB" /> Nahdonnis Praji, convinced that the Reborn Emperor had succumbed to delusions of grandeur, requested Kaikielius as a personal fief and left the Imperial Military, restoring House Praji's ancient connection to the planet.

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], Kaikielius was [[Invasion of Kaikielius|invaded]] by [[Yuuzhan Vong]] forces. The [[Praji Estate]] on Coruscant was destroyed when the Yuuzhan Vong [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|captured the planet]], and in the aftermath of the war House Praji relocated their holdings to Kaikielius, returning to their homeworld.<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

==Inhabitants==
Kaikielius' Human inhabitants were known as the Kaikielii. The planet was traditionally ruled by an aristocracy of Great Houses, of whom the greatest were the Triad of House Juoni, House Praji, and House Vahali, with many minor houses vying for power around them. Of the Triad, only House Praji achieved galactic importance, becoming a prominent political and [[Bank/Legends|banking]] family on Coruscant, with members in the [[Bank of the Core/Legends|Bank of the Core]], the [[Coruscant Ministry of Ingress/Legends|Coruscant Ministry of Ingress]], and Emppu Praji-Barck even becoming a [[Minister of State]].<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />

Of the other two Houses, the Juonii went extinct shortly after losing all their power in the [[First Alsakan Conflict]]. The Vahalii went on to control Kaikielius after the Prajii fled after the [[Quake Years]], and became the sole power on the planet in the aftermath of the Kaikieli Reconquista. Their space stations were destroyed by Nahdonnis Praji's fleet during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], and they were forced to flee into space. The Vahalii later re-established themselves on [[Denon/Legends|Denon]].<ref name="Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji" />
